title.zh: 卷359 列傳一百四十六 岳起 荆道乾 谢启昆 李殿图 张师诚 王绍兰 李奕畴 钱楷 和舜武
title.en: Volume 359 Biographies 146: Yue Qi, Jing Daoqian, Xie Qikun, Li Diantu, Zhang Shicheng, Wang Shaolan, Li Yichou, Qian Kai, He Shunwu
title.raw: 卷359 列傳一百四十六 岳起 荆道乾 谢启昆 李殿图 张师诚 王绍兰 李奕畴 钱楷 和舜武

sentences.zh: 列傳一百四十六

translations.literal: Biographies 146
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 146

sentences.zh: 岳起荊道乾謝啟昆李殿圖張師誠王紹蘭

translations.literal: Yue Qi, Jing Daoqian, Xie Qikun, Li Diantu, Zhang Shicheng, and Wang Shaolan
translations.idiomatic: Yue Qi, Jing Daoqian, Xie Qikun, Li Diantu, Zhang Shicheng, and Wang Shaolan

sentences.zh: 李奕疇錢楷和舜武

translations.literal: Li Yichou, Qian Kai, and He Shunwu
translations.idiomatic: Li Yichou, Qian Kai, and He Shunwu

sentences.zh: 岳起，鄂濟氏，滿洲鑲白旗人。

translations.literal: Yue Qi, of the Eji clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Qi, of the Eji clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十六年舉人，議敘，授筆帖式。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year of Qianlong he became a provincial graduate; after evaluation for service he was appointed a clerk (bitie shi).
translations.idiomatic: In 1771 he passed the provincial examinations; after his qualifications were reviewed, he was appointed a clerical secretary.

sentences.zh: 累擢戶部員外郎、翰林院侍講學士、詹事府少詹事。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Vice Commissioner in the Ministry of Revenue, Reader-in-Waiting in the Hanlin Academy, and Junior Vice Commissioner of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to become a vice commissioner in the Ministry of Revenue, a Hanlin reader-in-waiting, and junior vice commissioner of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，遷奉天府尹。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year he was transferred to be Governor of Fengtian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1791 he was appointed governor of Fengtian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 前官貪黷，岳起至，屋宇器用遍洗滌之，曰：「勿染其污跡也！

translations.literal: The previous official had been corrupt and venal; when Yue Qi arrived, he had all the buildings and furnishings thoroughly washed and cleaned, saying: "Do not let their filthy traces contaminate you!
translations.idiomatic: His predecessor had been corrupt; when Yue Qi took office, he had every room and piece of furniture scrubbed clean, saying, "Do not let their filth stain you!

sentences.zh: 」與將軍忤。

translations.literal: " He clashed with the general.
translations.idiomatic: " He soon came into conflict with the garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 逾年，擢內閣學士，尋出為江西布政使。

translations.literal: After a year he was promoted to Grand Secretariat Academician, and soon after was sent out as Jiangxi Provincial Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was promoted to grand secretariat academician, then posted as Jiangxi provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 殫心民事，值水災，行勘圩堤，落水致疾。

translations.literal: He devoted himself wholeheartedly to the people's affairs; when floods struck, he went out to inspect dikes and polders, fell into the water, and fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: He threw himself into local administration; during a flood he went to inspect dikes and polders, fell into the water, and took ill.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉其勤，許解任養疴。

translations.literal: An edict praised his diligence and permitted him to leave office to recuperate.
translations.idiomatic: The throne commended his diligence and allowed him to resign and recover his health.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，特起授山東布政使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he was specially recalled and appointed Shandong Provincial Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1799 he was specially recalled from retirement and appointed Shandong provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 未幾，擢江蘇巡撫。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Jiangsu Provincial Governor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to governor of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 清介自矢，僮僕僅數人，出屏騶從，禁遊船聲伎，無事不許宴賓演劇。

translations.literal: He held himself to strict integrity; he kept only a few servants, went out without escorts, forbade pleasure boats and entertainers, and allowed no banquets for guests or theatrical performances unless there was official business.
translations.idiomatic: He held himself to the strictest integrity, kept only a handful of servants, went out without a mounted escort, banned pleasure boats and musicians, and forbade banquets and theater except on official business.

sentences.zh: 吳下奢俗為之一變。

translations.literal: The extravagant customs of the Wu region were thereby transformed.
translations.idiomatic: The region's extravagant ways changed overnight.

sentences.zh: 疏陳漕弊，略曰：「京漕積習相因，惟弊是營。

translations.literal: He memorialized on abuses in the grain transport system, stating in summary: "The grain tribute to the capital has long-standing practices handed down through generations, and people devote themselves only to abuses.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial on abuses in the grain transport system, he wrote in part: "The tribute grain convoys to the capital are riddled with entrenched custom, and everyone profits from the abuses alone.

sentences.zh: 米數之盈絀，米色之純雜，竟置不問。

translations.literal: Whether the quantity of grain was surplus or short, and whether the grain was pure or mixed, they were entirely left unexamined.
translations.idiomatic: Shortfalls in quantity and adulteration in quality go entirely unchecked.

sentences.zh: 旗丁領運，無處不以米為挾制，即無處不以賄為通融。

translations.literal: Banner soldiers who led the transport used grain everywhere as a means of coercion, and used bribes everywhere as a means of accommodation.
translations.idiomatic: The banner transport crews use grain as leverage at every turn and bribes to smooth every obstacle.

sentences.zh: 推原其故，沿途之抑勒，由旗丁之有幫費；

translations.literal: Tracing the cause to its origin, the extortion along the route arose from the banner soldiers' receiving assistance fees;
translations.idiomatic: The root cause is clear: extortion along the route stems from the assistance fees demanded by the transport crews;

sentences.zh: 旗丁之索幫費，由州縣之浮收。

translations.literal: the banner soldiers' demanding of assistance fees arose from the districts' excessive collection.
translations.idiomatic: and those fees exist because counties and prefectures levy illegal surcharges.

sentences.zh: 除弊當絕其源，嚴禁浮收，實絕弊源之首。

translations.literal: To eliminate abuses one must cut off the source; strictly forbidding excessive collection is truly the foremost means of cutting off the source of abuses.
translations.idiomatic: To root out abuse you must cut off its source; a strict ban on illegal surcharges is the essential first step.

sentences.zh: 請下有漕各省，列款指明，嚴行禁革，俾旗丁及漕運倉場，無從更生觀望冀幸之心。

translations.literal: He requested that all provinces with grain transport be instructed to list items clearly and strictly prohibit and abolish them, so that banner soldiers and grain transport granaries would have no further occasion to harbor hopes of watching and waiting for advantage.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that every grain-transport province itemize prohibited charges and enforce the ban, so transport crews and granary officials would no longer hope to profit from the old ways.

sentences.zh: 」詔嘉其實心除弊。

translations.literal: " An edict praised his sincere-hearted effort to eliminate abuses.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne commended his earnest campaign against corruption.

sentences.zh: 常州知府胡觀瀾結交鹽政徵瑞長隨高柏林，派捐修葺江陰廣福寺。

translations.literal: Changzhou Prefect Hu Guanlan associated with Salt Commissioner Zheng Rui's chief attendant Gao Bolin and imposed levies to repair Jiangyin's Guangfu Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhou prefect Hu Guanlan, in league with salt commissioner Zheng Rui's chief attendant Gao Bolin, imposed levies to restore Guangfu Temple in Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 岳起疏言觀瀾、柏林雖罷逐，尚不足服眾心，請將錢二萬餘串責二人分償，以修蘇州官塘橋路。

translations.literal: Yue Qi memorialized that although Guanlan and Bolin had been dismissed and expelled, this was still insufficient to satisfy public sentiment; he requested that the more than twenty thousand strings of cash be charged to the two men to repay in shares, to repair Suzhou's official roads, bridges, and paths.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Qi argued that dismissing Hu and Gao was not enough to satisfy public outrage; he asked that they be ordered to repay jointly the more than twenty thousand strings of cash they had extorted, and that the money be used to repair Suzhou's official roads and bridges.

sentences.zh: 丹徒知縣黎誕登諷士紳臚其政績保留，實不職，劾罷之。

translations.literal: Dantu County Magistrate Li Yandeng induced the gentry to enumerate his administrative achievements for retention in office; in truth he was incompetent, and Yue Qi impeached and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: Dantu magistrate Li Yandeng had local gentry praise his record so he could remain in office, but Yue Qi found him unfit and had him removed.

sentences.zh: 五年，署兩江總督。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he served as acting Governor-General of Liangjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1800 he served as acting governor-general of Liangjiang.

sentences.zh: 劾南河工員莊剛、劉普等侵漁舞弊，莫澐於任所設店肆運貨至工居奇網利，並治如律。

translations.literal: He impeached Southern Canal engineering officials Zhuang Gang, Liu Pu, and others for embezzlement and fraud; Mo Yun had set up shops at his post, transported goods to the works to hoard and corner profits, and all were punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Southern Canal engineers Zhuang Gang, Liu Pu, and others for graft; Mo Yun had run shops from his post, shipping goods to worksites to corner profits—all were punished by law.

sentences.zh: 揚州關溢額稅銀不入私，盡以報解；

translations.literal: Surplus tax silver at Yangzhou Customs he did not take for himself but remitted in full;
translations.idiomatic: Surplus customs revenue at Yangzhou he kept none of for himself but remitted in full;

sentences.zh: 覈減兩籓司耗羨閒款，實存銀數報部：並下部議行。

translations.literal: he audited and reduced miscellaneous surplus funds of the two provincial treasuries and reported the actual silver on hand to the ministry: all were referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: he audited and cut surplus miscellaneous funds held by the two provincial treasuries and reported actual balances to the ministry—all referred to the ministries for implementation.

sentences.zh: 六年，疏請濬築毛城鋪以下河道堤岸、上游永城洪河、下游蕭、碭境內河堰，並藉帑舉工，分五年計畝徵還，允之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he memorialized requesting dredging and construction of river channels and dikes below Maochengpu, the upper Yongcheng Hong River, and lower Xia and Dang border interior river weirs, borrowing treasury funds to undertake the works and collecting repayment by mu over five years; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In 1801 he requested dredging and dike work below Maochengpu, on the upper Yongcheng Hong River, and on interior waterways in Xia and Dang, funded from the treasury and repaid by land assessment over five years; the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 八年，入覲，以疾留京，署禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he came to court for an audience, remained in the capital due to illness, and served as acting Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In 1803 he came to Beijing for an audience, remained there because of illness, and served as acting vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 會孝淑皇后奉移山陵，坐會疏措語不經，革職留任。

translations.literal: When Empress Xiaoshu was moved to her mountain tomb, he was punished because the joint memorial's wording was improper; he was stripped of office but retained in his post.
translations.idiomatic: During the transfer of Empress Xiaoshu's remains to the imperial tomb, he was demoted for improper wording in a joint memorial but kept at his post.

sentences.zh: 尋命解署職，遂卒。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to relinquish his acting post, and then he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon relieved of his acting appointment and died shortly afterward.

sentences.zh: 帝深惜之，贈太子少保，賜卹如例。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply regretted his loss, posthumously granted him Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and bestowed condolence payments according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him deeply, posthumously made him junior guardian of the heir apparent, and granted the usual funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 無子，詔問其家產，僅屋四間、田七十六畝。

translations.literal: He had no son; an edict inquired into his family property and found only four rooms of housing and seventy-six mu of land.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son; when the court inquired into his estate, it found only four rooms and seventy-six mu of land.

sentences.zh: 故事，旗員歿無嗣者產入官。

translations.literal: By precedent, when a banner official died without heirs his property entered official possession.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, when a bannerman died without heirs, his property reverted to the state.

sentences.zh: 以岳起家清貧，留贍其妻；

translations.literal: Because Yue Qi's family had been poor and upright, the property was retained to support his wife;
translations.idiomatic: Because Yue Qi's household had been so poor and upright, the estate was left to support his wife;

sentences.zh: 妻歿，官為管業，以為祭掃修墳之資。

translations.literal: when she died, the government managed the property as funds for sacrifices, tomb sweeping, and grave repair.
translations.idiomatic: and after her death the government managed it to fund sacrifices and upkeep of his tomb.

sentences.zh: 異數也。

translations.literal: This was an exceptional favor.
translations.idiomatic: Such treatment was wholly out of the ordinary.

sentences.zh: 妻亦嚴正，岳起為巡撫時，一日親往籍畢沅家。

translations.literal: His wife was also stern and upright; when Yue Qi was provincial governor, one day he went in person to inventory Bi Yuan's household.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was equally stern; while he was governor of Jiangsu, he once went in person to inventory the household of Bi Yuan.

sentences.zh: 暮歸，飲酒微醺。

translations.literal: Returning at dusk, he had drunk wine and was slightly tipsy.
translations.idiomatic: He came home at dusk slightly drunk.

sentences.zh: 妻正色曰：「畢公躭於酒色，不保其家，君方畏戒之不暇，乃復效彼耶？

translations.literal: His wife said sternly: "Master Bi was addicted to wine and women and could not preserve his household; you are just now too busy to fear and guard against this—will you now imitate him?
translations.idiomatic: His wife said sharply, "Bi Yuan drowned himself in wine and women and ruined his house—you ought to be on guard against that very example. Will you imitate him now?

sentences.zh: 」岳起謝之。

translations.literal: " Yue Qi apologized to her.
translations.idiomatic: " Yue Qi apologized at once.

sentences.zh: 及至京，居無邸舍，病歿於僧寺，妻紡績以終。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital he had no residence; he died of illness in a Buddhist temple, and his wife supported herself by spinning to the end.
translations.idiomatic: In Beijing he had no house; he died of illness in a monastery, and his wife lived out her days spinning thread.

sentences.zh: 吳民尤思其德，呼曰岳青天，演為歌謠，謂可繼湯斌雲。

translations.literal: The people of Wu especially remembered his virtue, calling him "Yue the Blue Heaven," composing songs about him, and saying he could succeed Tang Bin.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wu cherished his memory, called him "Justice Yue," set his praises in ballads, and said he stood in the line of Tang Bin.

sentences.zh: 荊道乾，字健中，山西臨晉人。

translations.literal: Jing Daoqian, style name Jianzhong, was a native of Linjin in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Daoqian, courtesy name Jianzhong, was from Linjin in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十四年舉人，大挑知縣，官湖南，歷麻陽、龍山、東安、永順、慈利、靖州。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Qianlong he became a provincial graduate; selected in the great assignment as county magistrate, he served in Hunan, successively at Mayang, Longshan, Dong'an, Yongshun, Cili, and Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial graduate of 1759, he was appointed county magistrate through the great assignment and served in Hunan at Mayang, Longshan, Dong'an, Yongshun, Cili, and Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 所至有惠政，屏陋規，平冤獄。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he had benevolent administration, rejected shabby regulations, and redressed wrongful convictions.
translations.idiomatic: Everywhere he served he brought real benefit, abolished petty abuses, and cleared wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 在靖州賑饑，尤多全活，屢膺上考。

translations.literal: At Jingzhou he relieved famine and especially saved many lives, repeatedly receiving top evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: At Jingzhou his famine relief saved countless lives, and he repeatedly earned top merit ratings.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，遷甘肅寧夏同知，入覲，大學士劉墉曾官湖南巡撫，稱之曰：「第一清官也。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year he was transferred to be Ningxia Subprefect in Gansu; when he came to audience, Grand Secretary Liu Yong, who had once been Hunan Provincial Governor, said of him: "The foremost incorrupt official.
translations.idiomatic: In 1782 he was transferred to Ningxia subprefect in Gansu; at court Grand Secretary Liu Yong, who had once governed Hunan, called him "the foremost honest official in the land.

sentences.zh: 」名始著。

translations.literal: " His reputation first became prominent.
translations.idiomatic: " His fame dates from that moment.

sentences.zh: 尋署石峰堡同知，時方用兵，治事不廢，修復水利，复薦卓異記名。

translations.literal: Soon he served as acting Shifengbao Subprefect; war was then underway, yet he did not neglect administration, restored water conservancy, and was again recommended as outstanding and placed on the roster.
translations.idiomatic: He soon acted as subprefect of Shifengbao; though the region was at war, he kept administration running, restored irrigation works, and was again marked for outstanding promotion.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，擢安徽池州知府，屢署徽寧池太道，筦蕪湖關，贏餘不入己，以充賑恤。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year he was promoted to Anhui Chizhou Prefect, repeatedly served as acting Huaining-Chizhou-Taiping Circuit intendant, managed Wuhu Customs, kept surpluses out of his own pocket, and used them for relief and charity.
translations.idiomatic: In 1789 he was promoted to prefect of Chizhou in Anhui, repeatedly acted as circuit intendant of Huai, Ning, Chi, and Tai, managed Wuhu customs, kept no surplus for himself, and devoted it all to relief.

sentences.zh: 調安慶，硃珪為巡撫，尤信任之，疏薦，擢山東登萊青道，攝布政使。

translations.literal: Transferred to Anqing, when Zhu Gui was provincial governor he especially trusted him, memorialized recommending him, and he was promoted to Shandong Dengzhou-Laizhou-Qingdao Circuit intendant, acting as provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Anqing, he won the deep trust of Governor Zhu Gui, who memorialized on his behalf; he was promoted to intendant of Deng, Lai, and Qing in Shandong and acted as provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 以激濁揚清為己任，薦廉吏崔映淮、李如珩等，而劾不飭者。

translations.literal: He took stirring the muddy and raising the clear as his duty, recommended incorrupt officials such as Cui Yinghuai and Li Ruheng, and impeached those who were undisciplined.
translations.idiomatic: He made it his mission to purge corruption and elevate the honest, recommending upright officials such as Cui Yinghuai and Li Ruheng while impeaching the undisciplined.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二年，遷按察使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiaqing he was transferred to Provincial Surveillance Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1797 he was appointed provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷江蘇布政使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Jiangsu Provincial Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1799 he became Jiangsu provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 先是州縣存留俸薪役食及驛站經費，改解籓庫，俟奏銷後請支，始則防吏侵挪，久之解有浮費，發有短平。

translations.literal: Previously the salaries, yamen runners' provisions, and courier station expenses retained by districts were changed to remittance to the provincial treasury, to be requested only after accounts were submitted for clearance; at first this was to prevent clerks' embezzlement, but over time remittance had surcharges and disbursement had shortfalls.
translations.idiomatic: Previously counties had remitted retained funds for salaries, runners, and courier stations to the provincial treasury and drawn them back only after accounts cleared—a reform meant to stop clerks from skimming, but over time remittances swelled with surcharges and disbursements fell short.

sentences.zh: 或勒抵前官虧空，佐雜教官不能得俸，驛傳領於臬司；

translations.literal: sometimes they were compelled to offset previous officials' deficits, assistant and miscellaneous educational officials could not receive salaries, and courier transport was managed by the surveillance commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Funds were sometimes seized to cover predecessors' deficits; junior educational officials went unpaid; courier expenses were controlled by the surveillance commissioner;

sentences.zh: 或苛駁案牘，因索餽遺，郵政日弛廢。

translations.literal: sometimes they harshly rejected documents and thereby demanded gifts; the postal service daily fell into decay.
translations.idiomatic: and documents were nitpicked to extort gifts, so the postal system decayed day by day.

sentences.zh: 道乾入覲時，面陳其弊，請悉依定章，於州縣徵收時開支，省解領之繁。

translations.literal: When Daoqian came to audience he stated these abuses in person and requested that all follow the established regulations, disbursing at the time of collection by districts, to spare the trouble of remitting and receiving.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing came to court he described these abuses in person and asked that disbursement follow the statutes at the county level, eliminating the round of remittance and reissue.

sentences.zh: 仁宗俞可；

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong approved;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong approved the proposal;

sentences.zh: 至是疏上施行，天下便之。

translations.literal: at this time he memorialized and it was implemented; the whole realm found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: and when he now put the reform into effect by memorial, the whole empire benefited.

sentences.zh: 上方欲整飭漕政，以巡撫岳起及道乾皆有清名，責其肅清諸弊。

translations.literal: The court above wished to rectify grain transport administration; because Provincial Governors Yue Qi and Daoqian both had reputations for integrity, it charged them to purge all abuses.
translations.idiomatic: The throne wished to reform the grain transport system and, because both Governor Yue Qi and Jing Daoqian were known for integrity, charged them to root out every abuse.

sentences.zh: 到官三閱月，擢安徽巡撫，疏請禁徵漕浮收舊耗米一斗，給運丁五升，加給二升。

translations.literal: Within three months of taking office he was promoted to Anhui Provincial Governor; he memorialized requesting prohibition of excessive grain transport surcharges, the old practice of one dou of wastage rice, giving transport soldiers five sheng, with an additional two sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Three months after taking office he was promoted to governor of Anhui and memorialized to ban illegal surcharges on tribute grain, fix the old wastage allowance at one dou, grant transport crews five sheng, and add two sheng more.

sentences.zh: 運丁所得，有據可考；

translations.literal: what the transport soldiers received had documentary basis for verification;
translations.idiomatic: What the transport crews received would be fixed and auditable;

sentences.zh: 其所用沿途浮費，採訪知之，應禁革。

translations.literal: the excessive fees they used along the route, known through investigation, should be prohibited and abolished.
translations.idiomatic: and every illegal fee along the route that investigation had uncovered should be abolished.

sentences.zh: 詔下所奏於有漕各省永禁。

translations.literal: An edict transmitted his memorial to all grain transport provinces for permanent prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered his recommendations permanently enforced in every grain-transport province.

sentences.zh: 又言：「屯田所以贍運，每丁派田若干及應得租耔，新僉旗丁不能了然。

translations.literal: He also stated: "Garrison fields exist to support transport; how many fields each soldier is assigned and what rent grain he should receive—newly enlisted banner soldiers cannot understand this clearly.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Garrison fields support the transport system, but newly enlisted banner crews cannot tell how much land each man holds or what rent is due.

sentences.zh: 令糧道刊刻木榜，俾僉丁認田收租。

translations.literal: Order the grain transport circuit intendant to carve wooden placards so enlisted soldiers can identify fields and collect rent.
translations.idiomatic: Have the grain intendant post carved wooden registers so each crew can identify its fields and collect rent.

sentences.zh: 運船領款，刻易知單，由丁正身親領，以杜包領欺壓之弊。

translations.literal: For transport boats receiving funds, carve easy-to-understand receipts so soldiers receive payment in person, to stop the abuse of proxy collection and oppression.
translations.idiomatic: Issue plain receipts for transport funds so each man collects payment in person, ending proxy collection and extortion.

sentences.zh: 田冊歸糧道收管，另造副冊發各衛以備查驗。

translations.literal: Field registers shall be kept by the grain transport intendant, with duplicate registers made and sent to each guard for inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Keep the master land registers with the grain intendant and issue duplicate copies to each guard for inspection.

sentences.zh: 」並允行。

translations.literal: " All were approved for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: " All were approved.

sentences.zh: 宿州、靈壁、泗州水災，道乾親往監視賑廠。

translations.literal: Suzhou, Lingbi, and Sizhou suffered flood disasters; Daoqian went in person to supervise relief stations.
translations.idiomatic: When floods struck Suzhou, Lingbi, and Sizhou, Jing went in person to oversee the relief depots.

sentences.zh: 六年，以病乞罷，詔許解任調理，俟病痊來京候簡。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, citing illness he requested dismissal; an edict permitted him to leave office to recuperate, and when recovered to come to the capital to await appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In 1801 he resigned on grounds of illness; the throne allowed him to leave office to recover and return to Beijing for reassignment when well.

sentences.zh: 次年三月，詔詢道乾病狀，已先卒於安慶，帝悼惜，賜祭，賜其孫炆舉人。

translations.literal: In the third month of the following year an edict inquired after Daoqian's illness; he had already died first at Anqing; the emperor mourned and regretted, bestowed sacrificial offerings, and granted his grandson Wen the status of provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: The following March the court inquired after his health—he had already died at Anqing. The emperor mourned him, ordered sacrifices, and granted his grandson Wen the status of provincial graduate.

sentences.zh: 道乾由監司不三年擢至巡撫，求治益急，不避嫌怨，自處刻苦。

translations.literal: Daoqian rose from surveillance and administration commissioner to provincial governor in less than three years; he sought good governance ever more urgently, did not avoid resentment and ill will, and treated himself with austerity.
translations.idiomatic: Jing rose from circuit commissioner to provincial governor in under three years, pressed ever harder for good government, shrank from no enmity, and lived in deliberate austerity.

sentences.zh: 臨歿，呼舊僚至寢所，指床下金示之曰：「吾受重恩，積養廉數千兩，足以歸喪。

translations.literal: On the verge of death he summoned old subordinates to his sleeping quarters, pointed to gold beneath the bed and showed them, saying: "I have received great favor and accumulated several thousand taels of integrity stipend, enough to return my coffin home.
translations.idiomatic: Near death he called old colleagues to his bedside, pointed to gold beneath it, and said, "I have received great favor from the throne and saved several thousand taels of my integrity stipend—enough to bear my coffin home.

sentences.zh: 諸君素愛我，勿為斂賻。

translations.literal: You gentlemen have always loved me—do not collect funeral contributions for me.
translations.idiomatic: You have always cared for me—do not collect funeral gifts on my behalf.

sentences.zh: 」又呼其兄曰：「兄仁弱，勿聽人慫恿受賻，違吾意。

translations.literal: " He also called his elder brother and said: "Elder brother, you are benevolent but weak—do not listen to people who urge you to accept gifts, going against my intent.
translations.idiomatic: " He then called his elder brother: "Brother, you are kind but weak—do not let anyone persuade you to accept funeral gifts against my wishes.

sentences.zh: 」兄如其言。

translations.literal: " His brother did as he said.
translations.idiomatic: " His brother obeyed.

sentences.zh: 謝啟昆，字蘊山，江西南康人。

translations.literal: Xie Qikun, style name Yunshan, was a native of Nankang in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Qikun, courtesy name Yunshan, was from Nankang in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 進士，朝考第一，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate, first in the palace examination, he was selected as a Hanlin bachelor and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi who ranked first in the palace examination, he entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 典河南鄉試，分校禮闈，均得士。

translations.literal: He presided over the Henan provincial examination and served as assistant examiner for the metropolitan civil examination; in both he obtained worthy scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He conducted the Henan provincial examinations and assisted in the metropolitan civil examinations, selecting able scholars in both.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，出為江蘇鎮江知府，調揚州。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he went out as Jiangsu Zhenjiang Prefect and was transferred to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1772 he was posted as prefect of Zhenjiang in Jiangsu, then transferred to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 明於吏事，所持堅正，上官異意不為奪。

translations.literal: He was clear in administrative affairs, held firm and upright principles, and was not swayed when superiors held different views.
translations.idiomatic: He was expert in administration, held his principles firmly, and would not bend when superiors disagreed.

sentences.zh: 治東台徐述夔詩詞悖逆獄遲緩，褫職戍軍台。

translations.literal: In handling the Dongtai Xu Shukui poetry treason case he was slow; he was stripped of office and banished to serve at a military post.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed and sent to garrison duty for moving too slowly in the Xu Shukui literary-treason case at Dongtai.

sentences.zh: 尋捐復原官，留江南。

translations.literal: Soon through donation he recovered his original office and remained in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He soon bought his way back to his former rank and remained in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 父憂，奪情署安徽寧國知府；

translations.literal: During mourning for his father he was recalled from mourning to serve as acting Anhui Ningguo Prefect;
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from mourning for his father, he acted as prefect of Ningguo in Anhui;

sentences.zh: 复遭母憂，服闋，稱病久不出。

translations.literal: he again suffered mourning for his mother; when mourning ended he claimed illness and long did not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: then mourned his mother; after mourning ended he pleaded illness and stayed out of office for years.

sentences.zh: 五十五年，特擢江南河庫道，遷浙江按察使。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year he was specially promoted to Jiangnan River Treasury Circuit intendant and transferred to Zhejiang Provincial Surveillance Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1790 he was specially promoted to intendant of the Jiangnan river treasury and then to Zhejiang surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 六十年，遷山西布政使。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year he was transferred to Shanxi Provincial Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1795 he became Shanxi provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 州縣倉庫積虧八十餘萬，不一歲悉補完。

translations.literal: District treasuries had accumulated deficits of more than eight hundred thousand, and within one year he made up all completely.
translations.idiomatic: County treasuries had run up deficits of more than eight hundred thousand taels; he made them up entirely within a year.

sentences.zh: 高宗異其才，以浙江財賦地虧尤多，特調任。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong marveled at his talent; because Zhejiang was a land of fiscal revenue where deficits were especially numerous, he was specially transferred there.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong admired his ability and, because Zhejiang's revenue deficits were especially severe, transferred him there specially.

sentences.zh: 歷三歲，亦彌補十之五。

translations.literal: Over three years he also made up five-tenths of them.
translations.idiomatic: In three years he made up half of those deficits as well.

sentences.zh: 廣西土司四十有六，生計日絀，貸於客民，輒以田產準折。

translations.literal: Guangxi had forty-six native chieftaincies; their livelihoods daily grew strained; they borrowed from settler commoners and always used their fields as standard for discount.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi had forty-six native chieftaincies whose livelihoods were failing; they borrowed from Han settlers and routinely pledged their land as collateral.

sentences.zh: 啟昆請禁重利盤剝，違者治罪。

translations.literal: Qikun requested prohibition of heavy interest and usury; violators were punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: Xie memorialized to ban usurious lending and punish violators.

sentences.zh: 田產給還土司，其無力回贖者，俟收田租滿一本一利，田歸原主，五年為斷；

translations.literal: Fields were returned to the native chieftains; those unable to redeem were to wait until collected field rent reached principal plus one profit, then fields returned to original owners, with five years as the limit;
translations.idiomatic: Land was returned to the chieftains; those unable to redeem might recover it once rent collected equaled principal plus interest, with a five-year limit after which title reverted;

sentences.zh: 其不禁客民入苗地者，廉土民馴愚，物產稀少，藉販運以通有無也。

translations.literal: As for not forbidding settler commoners to enter Miao territory, he considered the native people simple and foolish, products scarce, and relied on trade transport to exchange what was had and lacked.
translations.idiomatic: He did not ban Han traders from Miao lands because the natives were poor in goods and needed commerce to supply their wants.

sentences.zh: 仿浙江海塘竹簍囊石之法，修築興安陡河石堤，以除水患。

translations.literal: Following Zhejiang's seawall method of bamboo baskets filled with stone, he built stone dikes on Xing'an's Dou River to remove flood harm.
translations.idiomatic: He built stone dikes on the Dou River at Xing'an, using Zhejiang's wicker-basket revetment method, to control flooding.

sentences.zh: 河流深通，舊銅船過陡河必一月，至是三日而畢。

translations.literal: The river channel was deep and clear; formerly copper transport boats needed a full month to pass the Dou River; now it was completed in three days.
translations.idiomatic: Once the channel was dredged, copper transport boats that had needed a month to pass the Dou River could finish the run in three days.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒於官，詔嘉其廉潔，於所節省潯、梧兩關盈餘項下賜銀三千兩治喪。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died in office; an edict praised his integrity and cleanliness and granted three thousand taels of silver from surplus funds saved at Xun and Wu customs for funeral arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: In 1802 he died in office; the throne praised his integrity and granted three thousand taels from surpluses he had saved at the Xun and Wu customs posts for his funeral.

sentences.zh: 廣西士民請祀名宦祠。

translations.literal: Guangxi scholars and commoners requested his enshrinement in the shrine of renowned officials.
translations.idiomatic: The gentry and people of Guangxi petitioned to enshrine him in the local shrine of distinguished officials.

sentences.zh: 啟昆少以文學名，博聞強識，尤善為詩。

translations.literal: Qikun in youth was famed for literary learning, had wide knowledge and strong memory, and was especially skilled at poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Xie was known early for scholarship, possessed encyclopedic learning, and was an accomplished poet.

sentences.zh: 著《樹經堂集》、《西魏書》、《小學考》，晚成《廣西通志》，為世所稱。

translations.literal: He authored Collected Works from the Tree Classics Hall, History of Western Wei, and Studies in Elementary Learning; late in life he completed the Guangxi Gazetteer, all praised by the world.
translations.idiomatic: His works include the Shujingtang Collection, History of Western Wei, and Studies in Elementary Learning; late in life he finished the Guangxi Gazetteer, all highly regarded.

sentences.zh: 李殿圖，字桓符，直隸高陽人。

translations.literal: Li Diantu, style name Huanfu, was a native of Gaoyang in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Li Diantu, courtesy name Huanfu, was from Gaoyang in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十一年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate in the thirty-first year of Qianlong, he was selected as a Hanlin bachelor and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of 1766, he entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 典湖南鄉試，遷御史。

translations.literal: He presided over the Hunan provincial examination and was transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: He conducted the Hunan provincial examinations and was promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 督廣西學政，遷給事中。

translations.literal: He supervised Guangxi education, and was transferred to supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Guangxi education commissioner and was promoted to supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，甘肅回亂，從阿桂、福康安赴軍治糧餉、台站，授鞏秦階道。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year, during the Gansu Muslim rebellion, he followed Agui and Fuk'anggan to the army to manage provisions and courier stations, and was appointed Gong-Qin-Jie Circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In 1784, during the Gansu Muslim uprising, he joined Agui and Fuk'anggan's campaign to manage supplies and courier stations and was appointed intendant of Gong, Qin, and Jie.

sentences.zh: 軍事初竣，民、回相仇，焚掠報復，訛言時起。

translations.literal: When military affairs first concluded, Han and Muslim peoples were mutually hostile, burning and plundering in revenge, and false rumors constantly arose.
translations.idiomatic: When fighting ended, Han and Muslim communities turned on each other in arson, looting, and rumor.

sentences.zh: 殿圖處以鎮靜，叛黨緣坐，婦稚量情釋宥；

translations.literal: Diantu handled matters with calm; rebel associates implicated by connection, women and children were released according to circumstances;
translations.idiomatic: Li kept the situation calm, released women and children implicated by association with rebels when circumstances warranted,

sentences.zh: 罹害戶口，隨宜賑恤，流亡漸安。

translations.literal: households that had suffered harm were relieved as appropriate, and exiles gradually found peace.
translations.idiomatic: and gave relief to victim households until refugees gradually settled.

sentences.zh: 卓泥土司與四川松潘、漳臘各番爭噶噶固山界，殿圖輕騎履勘，歷小洮河、丈八嶺、鸚哥口，皆人跡罕到，群番導行，片語判決，立石達魚山頂而還。

translations.literal: Zhuotu native chieftain disputed the Gaga Gu Mountain boundary with the various tribes of Songpan and Zhangla in Sichuan; Diantu went on light horse to survey on foot, passing Xiaotao River, Zhangba Ridge, and Parrot Pass—all places rarely reached by human tracks—guided by the tribes, decided with a few words, erected a stone on Dayu Mountain summit, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhuotu chieftain disputed the Gaga Gu boundary with Songpan and Zhangla tribes, Li rode out to survey Xiaotao River, Zhangba Ridge, and Parrot Pass—almost untraveled country—guided by tribal leaders, settled the case in a few words, set a boundary marker on Dayu Peak, and returned.

sentences.zh: 高宗幾餘考涇、渭清濁源流，命殿圖親勘，自秦州溯流至鳥鼠、崆峒，繪圖附說以進，詔嘉其詳實。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong in his leisure studied the Jing and Wei rivers' clear and muddy sources; he ordered Diantu to survey in person, from Qinzhou upstream to Wushu and Kongtong, drew maps with explanatory notes and submitted them; an edict praised their detail and accuracy.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong had studied the sources of the Jing and Wei in his leisure and ordered Li to survey them in person from Qinzhou upstream to Wushu and Kongtong; his maps and report won imperial praise for their thoroughness.

sentences.zh: 六十年，遷福建按察使，嘉慶三年，就遷布政使。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year he was transferred to Fujian Provincial Surveillance Commissioner; in the third year of Jiaqing he was promoted in place to Provincial Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1795 he became Fujian surveillance commissioner; in 1798 he was promoted to provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「乾隆中，業農家必畜騾馬三四以任耕種，嗣後官吏借用應差，漸形滋擾，應嚴行革除。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "In the Qianlong period farming households necessarily kept three or four mules and horses for plowing; afterward officials borrowed them for corvée service, which gradually became harassment and should be strictly abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Under Qianlong, farming families kept several mules for plowing, but officials later commandeered them for corvée until the practice became intolerable and must be abolished.

sentences.zh: 獄訟必速為審結，開釋無辜，小民始得安業。

translations.literal: Lawsuits must be swiftly tried and concluded, the innocent released, and only then can common people settle in their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Cases must be tried promptly and the innocent released so common people can live in peace.

sentences.zh: 常平倉穀積久弊生，民未受益，官倉已受其虧。

translations.literal: Ever-normal granary grain over time accumulated abuses; the people did not benefit, while official granaries already suffered loss.
translations.idiomatic: Ever-normal granaries had grown corrupt over time—the people gained nothing while official stores bled losses.

sentences.zh: 無災之年，不宜貸假。

translations.literal: In years without disaster, lending should not be made.
translations.idiomatic: In years without disaster, grain should not be lent out.

sentences.zh: 吏役例有定額，近則人思託足，藉免役徭。

translations.literal: Clerks and runners had fixed quotas by regulation; recently people sought to lodge themselves under them to escape corvée and levies.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks and runners had fixed quotas, but lately people sought posts under them to escape corvée.

sentences.zh: 關津稅口，官署長隨，呼朋引類，並為奸藪，宜並禁止。

translations.literal: At tax passes and ferry crossings, yamen chief attendants gathered companions and drew in their kind, all becoming nests of villainy, and all should be prohibited together.
translations.idiomatic: At customs posts and ferries, yamen attendants formed gangs of extortionists—all should be banned.

sentences.zh: 」詔下直省一體察禁。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered all provinces to investigate and prohibit together.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict ordered every province to investigate and enforce the ban.

sentences.zh: 閩俗售田，田面田根，糾纏不決。

translations.literal: Fujian custom in selling fields distinguished surface rights and root rights, entangled without resolution.
translations.idiomatic: In Fujian, land sales split surface rights from underlying title, breeding endless disputes.

sentences.zh: 蠹吏影射，佃戶頑抗，錢糧日多脫欠，徵收不敷，每以虛出通關而致虧缺，殿圖奏請嚴治。

translations.literal: Corrupt clerks made shadow references, tenants stubbornly resisted, land tax daily grew in arrears, collection fell short, and often fictitious clearance passes caused deficits; Diantu memorialized requesting strict punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt clerks exploited the confusion, tenants resisted payment, tax arrears mounted, and false clearance receipts caused deficits—Li memorialized for strict enforcement.

sentences.zh: 在任逾年，庫儲大增。

translations.literal: Within a year in office, treasury stores greatly increased.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year, provincial reserves grew substantially.

sentences.zh: 擢安徽巡撫，七年，調福建。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Anhui Provincial Governor; in the seventh year he was transferred to Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to governor of Anhui; in 1802 he was transferred to Fujian.

sentences.zh: 有林、陳、藍、胡諸大姓糾眾械鬥，治如律。

translations.literal: The great clans Lin, Chen, Lan, and Hu gathered crowds for armed fights; he punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: When the Lin, Chen, Lan, and Hu clans mobilized for armed feuds, he punished them by law.

sentences.zh: 治海盜三腳虎及蔡牽羽黨，請祀海洋陣亡官兵，緝匪死事者一體入祀，從之。

translations.literal: He dealt with the pirates Three-Legged Tiger and Cai Qian's followers, requested enshrinement of officers and soldiers who died in battle at sea, and that those who died in pursuit of bandits be enshrined together; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed the pirate Three-Legged Tiger and Cai Qian's followers, petitioned to enshrine officers killed at sea and those who died hunting bandits together—the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 十一年，蔡牽久未平，仁宗以台灣剿捕事殷，殿圖操守尚好，軍務未嫺，調江西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Cai Qian had long gone unpacified; Emperor Renzong, because Taiwan suppression affairs were pressing, and Diantu's integrity was still good but he was not skilled in military affairs, transferred him to Jiangxi Provincial Governor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1806, with Cai Qian still at large and Taiwan operations urgent, the emperor transferred Li to Jiangxi—his integrity was sound, but he lacked military experience.

sentences.zh: 尋詔斥殿圖於軍事無所陳奏，又不能禁止海口偷漏水米火藥，降四五品京堂；

translations.literal: Soon an edict rebuked Diantu for making no memorials on military affairs and being unable to stop smuggling of grain, gunpowder, and other goods at the seaports; he was demoted to fourth- or fifth-rank capital official;
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict rebuked him for silence on military affairs and failure to stop smuggling of grain and gunpowder at the coast; he was demoted to a fourth- or fifth-rank capital post;

sentences.zh: 又以所屬久羈案犯，以中允、贊善降補。

translations.literal: also because his subordinates long detained case prisoners, he was demoted to supplemental middle attendant and expositor.
translations.idiomatic: and further demoted to middle attendant and expositor because his subordinates had long detained prisoners without trial.

sentences.zh: 尋遷翰林院侍講，引病歸。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Hanlin Academy Reader-in-Waiting and returned home citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Hanlin reader-in-waiting, then retired citing illness.

sentences.zh: 十七年，卒。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1812.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，閩浙總督文煜疏陳殿圖前任福建政績昭著，諡文肅。

translations.literal: In early Guangxu, Fujian-Zhejiang Governor-General Wen Yu memorialized that Diantu's former administration in Fujian had outstanding achievements, and he was given the posthumous title Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangxu reign, Governor-General Wen Yu memorialized Li's distinguished record in Fujian, and he was posthumously titled Wensu.

sentences.zh: 張師誠，字蘭渚，浙江歸安人。

translations.literal: Zhang Shicheng, style name Lanzhu, was a native of Gui'an in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shicheng, courtesy name Lanzhu, was from Gui'an in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 乾隆中，南巡，召試賜舉人，授內閣中書，充軍機章京。

translations.literal: During Qianlong's southern tour he was summoned for examination, granted provincial graduate status, appointed Grand Secretariat Secretary, and served as Grand Council clerk.
translations.idiomatic: During Qianlong's southern tour he passed a special examination, was granted juren status, appointed grand secretariat secretary, and served on the Grand Council staff.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部主事，忤和珅，緣事降中書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Department Director in the Ministry of Personnel, offended Heshen, and was demoted to secretary on a related matter.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to director in the Ministry of Personnel, he offended Heshen and was demoted to secretary.

sentences.zh: 得應會試，五十五年，成進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: He became eligible for the metropolitan examination; in the fifty-fifth year he became a metropolitan graduate, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Eligible again for the metropolitan examinations, he became a jinshi in 1790, entered the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，出為山西蒲州知府，歷雁平道，河南、江蘇按察使，遷山西布政使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing he went out as Shanxi Puzhou Prefect, served as Yanping Circuit intendant, Henan and Jiangsu Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, and was transferred to Shanxi Provincial Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1796 he was posted as prefect of Puzhou in Shanxi, then served as Yanping intendant and surveillance commissioner in Henan and Jiangsu before becoming Shanxi provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 州縣倉庫多虧，師誠知清查有名無實，特嚴於交代之際，有虧必完，在任三年，庫儲充裕。

translations.literal: District treasuries had many deficits; Shicheng knew that audits were nominal without substance, and was especially strict at handover—where there was deficit it must be made up; in three years in office, treasury stores were ample.
translations.idiomatic: County treasuries were deeply in deficit; Zhang knew audits were hollow and enforced strict settlement at every handover—any shortfall had to be made good—and within three years provincial reserves were full.

sentences.zh: 十一年，擢江西巡撫，以兼提督賜花翎，遂著為令。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was promoted to Jiangxi Provincial Governor; because he also held the post of provincial military commander he was granted the peacock feather, which thereafter became a regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In 1806 he was promoted to governor of Jiangxi; because he also served as provincial military commander he received the peacock feather—a precedent thereafter.

sentences.zh: 尋調福建，清治淹牘，疏陳整頓積弊事宜，詔嘉勉。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Fujian, cleared accumulated documents, memorialized on rectifying long-standing abuses, and an edict praised and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon transferred to Fujian, he cleared the backlog of cases, memorialized on rooting out entrenched abuses, and won imperial commendation.

sentences.zh: 時海盜蔡牽、硃濆方猖獗，總督玉德廢弛黜去，阿林保繼任，復與​​提督李長庚不協；

translations.literal: At the time the pirates Cai Qian and Zhu Fen were raging; Governor-General Yude was dismissed for laxness; Alinbao succeeded him but again was at odds with Provincial Military Commander Li Changeng;
translations.idiomatic: Pirates Cai Qian and Zhu Fen were then rampant; Governor-General Yude was dismissed for negligence; his successor Alinbao clashed with Admiral Li Changeng;

sentences.zh: 師誠至，始嚴防海口，杜岸姦接濟，籌備船械，長庚得盡力剿捕。

translations.literal: when Shicheng arrived, he first strictly guarded the seaports, stopped shore collusion in supplying the enemy, prepared boats and weapons, and Changeng was able to exert full effort in pursuit and capture.
translations.idiomatic: when Zhang arrived he sealed the coastal ports, cut off shore supplies to the pirates, equipped the fleet, and Li Changeng could pursue them in earnest.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，長庚追蔡牽於粵洋，以傷殞。

translations.literal: That winter Changeng pursued Cai Qian in Guangdong waters and died of wounds.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Li Changeng pursued Cai Qian in Guangdong waters and died of his wounds.

sentences.zh: 牽犯台灣後山噶仔蘭，為生番擊退，請收其地入版籍，免為賊踞。

translations.literal: Qian invaded Gazilan on Taiwan's eastern rear mountains, was repelled by raw barbarians, and Zhang requested bringing the territory into the registered domain so it would not be occupied by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Cai raided Gazilan on eastern Taiwan, was driven off by indigenous tribes, and Zhang petitioned to bring the territory under Qing administration lest pirates seize it.

sentences.zh: 十三年，硃濆與牽有隙，獨竄閩洋，總兵許松年擊斃之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Zhu Fen had a rift with Qian and alone fled into Fujian waters; Regional Commander Xu Songnian struck and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1808 Zhu Fen broke with Cai Qian and fled alone into Fujian waters, where Regional Commander Xu Songnian killed him.

sentences.zh: 其弟渥，勢蹙思投首，會道員德華由台灣內渡，遇牽黨圍劫，渥救之，藉以通款，尋复拒敵粵師不果降。

translations.literal: His younger brother Wo, pressed hard, wished to surrender; when Circuit Intendant Dehua crossed from Taiwan inland, he encountered Qian's party surrounding and robbing him; Wo rescued him and used this to open communications, but soon again resisted Guangdong troops and surrender did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Wo, cornered, wished to surrender; when Circuit Intendant Dehua crossed from Taiwan, Wo rescued him from Cai's men and opened negotiations, but soon fought Guangdong forces again and the surrender failed.

sentences.zh: 十四年，阿林保調兩江，師誠暫署總督。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Alinbao was transferred to Liangjiang, and Shicheng temporarily served as acting governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In 1809 Alinbao was transferred to Liangjiang, and Zhang acted as governor-general.

sentences.zh: 聞蔡牽竄浙洋，親駐廈門，提督王得祿、邱良功合剿，毀盜舟，牽墮海死。

translations.literal: Hearing Cai Qian had fled into Zhejiang waters, he personally stationed at Xiamen; Provincial Military Commanders Wang Delu and Qiu Lianggong jointly pursued, destroyed pirate boats, and Qian fell into the sea and died.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Cai Qian had entered Zhejiang waters, he took post at Xiamen; Admirals Wang Delu and Qiu Lianggong joined the pursuit, destroyed the pirate fleet, and Cai fell into the sea and drowned.

sentences.zh: 硃渥尋率三千餘人歸誠，赦其罪，海疆以安，閩人刊石烏石山以紀功。

translations.literal: Zhu Wo soon led more than three thousand men to submit in good faith; their crimes were pardoned, the maritime frontier was pacified, and Fujian people carved stone on Wushi Mountain to record the achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wo soon surrendered with more than three thousand followers; their crimes were pardoned, the coast was pacified, and the people of Fujian carved a monument on Wushi Mountain to commemorate the victory.

sentences.zh: 海寇稽誅久，由閩、浙不能合力，自師誠治閩，而阮元復蒞浙，始告成功。

translations.literal: Sea bandits had long delayed punishment because Fujian and Zhejiang could not combine forces; from the time Shicheng governed Fujian and Ruan Yuan again took Zhejiang, success was finally announced.
translations.idiomatic: Sea pirates had long eluded capture because Fujian and Zhejiang could not coordinate; only when Zhang governed Fujian and Ruan Yuan took Zhejiang did the campaign finally succeed.

sentences.zh: 仁宗嘉其嚴斷接濟，為殄寇之本。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong praised his strict cutting off of supplies as the foundation for exterminating bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong praised his strict blockade of pirate supplies as the key to destroying the enemy.

sentences.zh: 京察特予獎敘。

translations.literal: At the capital evaluation he was specially granted commendation and promotion.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital personnel review he received special commendation.

sentences.zh: 十九年，調江蘇。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was transferred to Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1814 he was transferred to Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 百齡為總督，諸巡撫皆承望風旨，師誠獨舉其職。

translations.literal: Bailing was governor-general; all provincial governors followed his wind and intent, but Shicheng alone performed his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Bai Ling dominated the province, and other governors followed his lead—only Zhang performed his duties independently.

sentences.zh: 初彭齡奉命同查虧帑，意與百齡、師誠不合，遂劾兩人皆受餽遺，而不得實，詔原之。

translations.literal: Initially Peng Ling was ordered to jointly investigate treasury deficits; his views did not agree with Bailing and Shicheng, so he impeached both for receiving gifts, but could not substantiate it; an edict pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: When Peng Ling was ordered to investigate treasury deficits, he clashed with Bai and Zhang and impeached both for taking gifts—but could not prove it, and the throne pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 會百齡窮治逆書獄，閭閻悚息，巡撫所主五府州得無擾。

translations.literal: When Bailing rigorously prosecuted the treasonous writings case, lanes and wards trembled in fear, but the five prefectures and departments under the governor's charge were not disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: While Bai Ling pursued the literary-treason cases relentlessly, the five prefectures under Zhang's jurisdiction were spared the terror.

sentences.zh: 川沙民有燒香傳徒者，有司密捕解江寧，師誠遣標弁要於途，交按察司依律鞫治，免辜磔者數十人，時以稱之。

translations.literal: Chuansha commoners had incense-burning transmission of disciples; officials secretly arrested and sent them to Jiangning; Shicheng dispatched armed runners to intercept on the road and hand them to the surveillance commissioner for trial according to law, sparing several dozen innocent people from execution by dismemberment; contemporaries praised this.
translations.idiomatic: When officials secretly arrested Chuansha sectarians bound for Nanjing, Zhang sent runners to intercept them and had the surveillance commissioner try the case by law, sparing dozens from execution—an act widely praised.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，父病篤，不俟代回籍，被嚴議褫職。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year his father was gravely ill; without waiting for a successor he returned to his native place and was severely criticized and stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1816 his father fell gravely ill; he left office without waiting for a successor and was stripped of his post after severe censure.

sentences.zh: 尋予編修，服闋，遷中允。

translations.literal: Soon he was granted the post of compiler; when mourning ended he was transferred to middle attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored as compiler; after mourning he was promoted to middle attendant.

sentences.zh: 歷江西、安徽布政使。

translations.literal: He served as Jiangxi and Anhui Provincial Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served as provincial administration commissioner in Jiangxi and Anhui.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，擢廣東巡撫，調安徽，繼母憂去官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he was promoted to Guangdong Provincial Governor, transferred to Anhui, and left office on mourning for his stepmother.
translations.idiomatic: In 1821 he was promoted to governor of Guangdong, transferred to Anhui, and resigned on mourning for his stepmother.

sentences.zh: 复歷山西、江蘇巡撫。

translations.literal: He again served as Shanxi and Jiangsu Provincial Governor.
translations.idiomatic: He later served again as governor of Shanxi and Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 六年，召授倉場侍郎。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of the Granary Fields.
translations.idiomatic: In 1826 he was summoned and appointed vice minister of the granary fields.

sentences.zh: 以病乞歸，卒於家。

translations.literal: Citing illness he requested to return home and died at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: He retired citing illness and died at home.

sentences.zh: 師誠警敏綜覈，在當時疆吏中有能名，治福建最著，繼之者為王紹蘭。

translations.literal: Shicheng was alert, keen, and comprehensive in investigation; among frontier officials of the time he had a reputation for ability, and his governance of Fujian was most renowned; his successor was Wang Shaolan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang was sharp and thorough; among frontier officials of his day he was famed for ability, above all in Fujian—where Wang Shaolan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 紹蘭，字南陔，浙江蕭山人。

translations.literal: Wang Shaolan, style name Nangai, was a native of Xiaoshan in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shaolan, courtesy name Nangai, was from Xiaoshan in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十八年進士，授福建南屏知縣，調閩縣。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate in the fifty-eighth year of Qianlong, he was appointed Fujian Nanping County Magistrate and transferred to Min County.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of 1793, he was appointed magistrate of Nanping in Fujian, then transferred to Min County.

sentences.zh: 巡撫汪志伊薦其治行，仁宗曰：「王紹蘭好官，朕早聞其名。

translations.literal: Provincial Governor Wang Zhiyi recommended his administrative conduct; Emperor Renzong said: "Wang Shaolan is a good official; I have long heard his name.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Wang Zhiyi recommended his record; Emperor Renzong said, "Wang Shaolan is an excellent official—I have long known his name.

sentences.zh: 」召入見，以知州用，擢泉州知府。

translations.literal: " He was summoned for an audience, used as a prefect, and promoted to Quanzhou Prefect.
translations.idiomatic: " He was summoned to court, appointed a prefect, and promoted to prefect of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 漳、泉兩郡多械鬥，自紹蘭治泉州，民俗漸馴，而漳州守令以械鬥獄獲罪，詔舉紹蘭以為法。

translations.literal: Zhang and Quan two prefectures had many armed fights; from the time Shaolan governed Quanzhou, local customs gradually grew tame, while Zhangzhou prefects and magistrates were punished for armed-fight cases; an edict held up Shaolan as the model.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang and Quan were rife with clan feuds; under Wang at Quanzhou customs grew tame, while Zhangzhou officials were punished for feuds—an edict held Wang up as the model.

sentences.zh: 擢興泉永道，捕獲蔡牽養子蔡三及其黨蔡昌等，予議敘。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Xing-Quan-Yong Circuit intendant, captured Cai Qian's adopted son Cai San and his follower Cai Chang and others, and was granted deliberation for commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to intendant of Xing, Quan, and Yong, he captured Cai Qian's adopted son Cai San and follower Cai Chang and was recommended for reward.

sentences.zh: 遷按察使，母憂去，服闋，起故官，就遷布政使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, left on mourning for his mother, and when mourning ended resumed his former office and was promoted in place to Provincial Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He became surveillance commissioner, left on mourning for his mother, and after mourning resumed office and was promoted to provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十九年，擢巡撫，始終未出福建。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Jiaqing he was promoted to Provincial Governor and never left Fujian to the end.
translations.idiomatic: In 1814 he was promoted to governor and never left Fujian.

sentences.zh: 尋汪志伊來為​​總督，與布政使李賡芸不合，因訐告受賂，劾治，屬吏希指羅織，賡芸憤而自縊。

translations.literal: Soon Wang Zhiyi came as governor-general; he did not agree with Provincial Administration Commissioner Li Gengyun, and because of mutual accusations of taking bribes impeached and prosecuted him; subordinate officials followed cues to entangle and fabricate charges, and Gengyun in anger hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wang Zhiyi arrived as governor-general, clashed with Administration Commissioner Li Gengyun, and impeached him for bribery; subordinates fabricated charges, and Li hanged himself in despair.

sentences.zh: 志伊獲譴，紹蘭坐不能匡正，牽連罷職。

translations.literal: Zhiyi received punishment; Shaolan was punished for being unable to correct matters and was implicated and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhiyi was punished; Wang Shaolan was dismissed for failing to restrain him.

sentences.zh: 少嗜學，究經史大義。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning and investigated the great principles of the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning and pursued the great themes of the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 去官後，一意著述，以許慎、鄭康成為宗，於儀禮、說文致力尤深，著書皆可傳。

translations.literal: After leaving office he devoted himself entirely to writing, took Xu Shen and Zheng Xuan as his masters, and applied especially deep effort to the Book of Etiquette and Ceremonies and Explaining Graphs; his books are all worthy of transmission.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving office he devoted himself to scholarship, took Xu Shen and Zheng Xuan as models, and wrote enduring works on the Book of Rites and the Shuowen.

sentences.zh: 李奕疇，字書年，河南夏邑人。

translations.literal: Li Yichou, style name Shunian, was a native of Xiayi in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yichou, courtesy name Shunian, was from Xiayi in Henan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十五年進士，選庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate in the forty-fifth year of Qianlong, he was selected as a Hanlin bachelor and appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of 1780, he entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor and was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 大考改禮部主事，典貴州鄉試，洊遷郎中。

translations.literal: In the great examination he was transferred to Department Director in the Ministry of Rites, presided over the Guizhou provincial examination, and was repeatedly promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: After a strong palace examination he became a director in the Ministry of Rites, conducted the Guizhou provincial examinations, and rose to bureau director.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，出為山西寧武知府，調平陽，有政聲。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year he went out as Shanxi Ningwu Prefect, was transferred to Pingyang, and had a reputation for good administration.
translations.idiomatic: In 1792 he was posted as prefect of Ningwu in Shanxi, then transferred to Pingyang, earning a reputation for good government.

sentences.zh: 歷江蘇糧道、山東按察使。

translations.literal: He served as Jiangsu Grain Transport Circuit intendant and Shandong Provincial Surveillance Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served as grain transport intendant in Jiangsu and surveillance commissioner in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十一年，坐巡撫保薦屬吏違例，牽連被議，左遷江南河庫道。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Jiaqing he was punished because a provincial governor's recommendation of a subordinate official violated regulations; implicated and criticized, he was demoted to Jiangnan River Treasury Circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In 1806 he was demoted to Jiangnan river treasury intendant for irregularities in a governor's recommendation of a subordinate.

sentences.zh: 十三年，遷安徽按察使，治獄明慎，多平反。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to Anhui Provincial Surveillance Commissioner; he handled cases clearly and cautiously and reversed many wrongful convictions.
translations.idiomatic: In 1808 he became Anhui surveillance commissioner, tried cases with care, and reversed many wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 霍丘民範受之者，贅於顧氏，與妻反目，外出久不歸。

translations.literal: Huaiqiu commoner Fan Shouzhi had married into the Gu family as a live-in son-in-law, quarreled with his wife, and went away for a long time without returning.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Shouzhi of Huoqiu had married into the Gu family, quarreled with his wife, and left home for a long absence.

sentences.zh: 縣令誤聽訛言，謂其妻私於鄰楊三，鍛鍊成獄，當顧氏、楊三謀殺罪，其母與弟及傭工某加功，實無左證，五人者不勝刑，皆誣服。

translations.literal: The county magistrate mistakenly listened to false rumors, saying his wife had an affair with neighbor Yang San, forged a case, convicted the Gu woman and Yang San of conspiracy to murder, with his mother, younger brother, and a hired laborer as accomplices; in truth there was no corroborating evidence; the five persons could not endure torture and all falsely confessed.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate believed rumors that Fan's wife had an affair with a neighbor named Yang San, fabricated a murder case against the Gu family, Yang, Fan's mother, his brother, and a servant—and with no real evidence, all five confessed under torture.

sentences.zh: 奕疇閱供詞，疑之，驟詰曰：「爾曹言骨已被焚，然尚有臟腑腸胃，棄之何所？

translations.literal: Yichou read the confessions, doubted them, and suddenly questioned: "You say the bones were already burned, yet there were still viscera and intestines—where were they discarded?
translations.idiomatic: Reading the confessions, Li grew suspicious and suddenly demanded, "You say the body was burned—but what of the organs and entrails? Where were they thrown?

sentences.zh: 」囚不能對，惟伏地哭。

translations.literal: " The prisoners could not answer and only prostrated themselves weeping.
translations.idiomatic: " The prisoners could not answer and only wept on the floor.

sentences.zh: 奕疇慨然曰：「是有冤！

translations.literal: Yichou said with emotion: "There is injustice here!
translations.idiomatic: Li exclaimed, "This is a wrongful case!

sentences.zh: 」使幹吏偵之，至陳姓家，言正月十五夜受之曾過宿，而讞曰被殺在十三日，乃緩系諸囚，嚴緝受之。

translations.literal: " He sent capable clerks to investigate; at the Chen household they said that on the night of the fifteenth of the first month Shouzhi had stayed over, while the verdict said he was killed on the thirteenth; he then eased detention of the prisoners and strictly pursued Shouzhi.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent investigators to the Chen household, who reported Fan had stayed there on the fifteenth of the first month—two days after the alleged murder on the thirteenth. Li eased the prisoners' confinement and hunted for Fan.

sentences.zh: 久之，受之忽自歸，則以負博遠避，不敢使家人知所在，今始聞大獄起，乃歸投案也。

translations.literal: After a long time Shouzhi suddenly returned on his own; he had fled far because of gambling debts, dared not let his family know where he was, and only now heard the great case had arisen, so he returned to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually Fan returned of his own accord—he had fled to escape gambling debts without telling his family, and came back only when he heard of the capital case.

sentences.zh: 事得白。

translations.literal: The matter was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: The truth came out and the innocent were freed.

sentences.zh: 奕疇故無子，獄既解，乃生子銘皖。

translations.literal: Yichou had formerly had no son; once the case was resolved, he then had a son Mingwan.
translations.idiomatic: Li had been childless; after the case was cleared, his wife bore a son named Mingwan.

sentences.zh: 民間傳頌，至演為劇曲。

translations.literal: Among the people it was passed down in praise, even performed as opera.
translations.idiomatic: The story spread among the people and even became an opera.

sentences.zh: 就遷布政使。

translations.literal: He was then promoted in place to Provincial Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十八年，擢浙江巡撫。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to Zhejiang Provincial Governor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1813 he was promoted to governor of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 時近畿教匪未靖，或言嚴、衢兩郡匪徒傳習天罡會，詔奕疇嚴治。

translations.literal: At the time sect rebels in the metropolitan periphery were not yet pacified; some said bandits in Yan and Qu two prefectures transmitted practice of the Tiangan Society; an edict ordered Yichou to punish strictly.
translations.idiomatic: With sect unrest still near the capital, reports claimed bandits in Yan and Qu were practicing the Tiangan Society; the throne ordered Li to crack down.

sentences.zh: 奕疇逮訊葉機、姚漢楫等，實止愚民相聚誦經祈福，無逆跡，坐罪首犯數人，株連皆省釋。

translations.literal: Yichou arrested and interrogated Ye Ji, Yao Hanji, and others; in truth it was only foolish people gathering to chant sutras and pray for blessings, with no treasonous traces; he convicted only a few chief offenders and released all implicated by connection.
translations.idiomatic: Li arrested Ye Ji, Yao Hanji, and others and found only peasants gathering to chant sutras for blessings—no treason. He punished a few ringleaders and released everyone else.

sentences.zh: 安徽、江西遊民來浙租山墾種者日眾，言官請禁。

translations.literal: Wandering people from Anhui and Jiangxi coming to Zhejiang to rent mountains for reclamation and planting grew daily in number; censorial officials requested prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: Anhui and Jiangxi migrants renting mountain land in Zhejiang grew daily, and censors called for a ban.

sentences.zh: 奕疇疏陳勢難遽逐，請分年遣令回籍。

translations.literal: Yichou memorialized that the situation made sudden expulsion difficult and requested sending them back to their native places over several years.
translations.idiomatic: Li memorialized that sudden expulsion was impractical and asked to send them home over several years.

sentences.zh: 上悟曰：「茲事不易言。

translations.literal: The emperor understood and said: "This matter is not easy to speak of.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "This is no simple matter.

sentences.zh: 遊民皆無恆產，驅之此省，又轉徙他省，斷不能復歸鄉里。

translations.literal: Wandering people all lack fixed property; drive them from this province and they shift to another, and certainly cannot return to their home districts.
translations.idiomatic: These people have no fixed livelihood; drive them from one province and they move to another—they can never return home.

sentences.zh: 」命徐謀教養，俾流亡者變為土著，乃得安。

translations.literal: " He ordered gradual planning for nurture and education so exiles became natives, and only then could there be peace.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered gradual settlement and support so migrants became locals—that alone would bring stability.

sentences.zh: 尋授漕運總督，在任五年，運務無誤。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Grain Transport Governor-General; in five years in office transport duties had no errors.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed grain transport governor-general and ran the service flawlessly for five years.

sentences.zh: 奕疇固長者，待下寬，坐濫委運弁降四級，命以吏、禮二部郎中用。

translations.literal: Yichou was by nature a senior worthy man and lenient to subordinates; he was punished for indiscriminately delegating transport officers, demoted four ranks, and ordered to serve as director in the Ministries of Personnel and Rites.
translations.idiomatic: A kindly man who treated subordinates leniently, he was demoted four ranks for lax delegation of transport officers and appointed director in the Ministries of Personnel and Rites.

sentences.zh: 復以運弁縱容幫丁索費，被劾，降主事。

translations.literal: Again because transport officers indulged assistance soldiers in demanding fees, he was impeached and demoted to department director.
translations.idiomatic: He was again impeached and demoted to department director when transport officers let crews extort assistance fees.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，宣宗即位，命奕疇以尚書守護昌陵。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year Emperor Xuanzong took the throne and ordered Yichou as Minister to guard Changling.
translations.idiomatic: In 1825 Emperor Xuanzong ascended the throne and appointed Li minister to guard Changling Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 道光二年，原品休致。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he retired at his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: In 1822 he retired at his original rank.

sentences.zh: 十九年，重宴鹿鳴，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was again feasted at the Luming banquet and made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1839 he was honored at a second Luming banquet and made junior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 明年，會榜重逢，子銘皖適登第，同與恩榮宴，稱盛事焉。

translations.literal: The next year the metropolitan examination list was met again; his son Mingwan happened to pass the examinations, and father and son together attended the grace and glory banquet—a thing called a grand occasion.
translations.idiomatic: The following year his son Mingwan passed the metropolitan examinations, and father and son attended the imperial banquet together—a celebrated occasion.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，卒，年九十有一。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he died, aged ninety-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1844 at the age of ninety-one.

sentences.zh: 錢楷，字裴山，浙江嘉興人。

translations.literal: Qian Kai, style name Peishan, was a native of Jiaxing in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Kai, courtesy name Peishan, was from Jiaxing in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十四年進士，選翰林院庶吉士，散館改戶部主事，充軍機章京。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate in the fifty-fourth year of Qianlong, he was selected as a Hanlin bachelor; after leaving the academy he was made Department Director in the Ministry of Revenue and served as Grand Council clerk.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of 1789, he entered the Hanlin Academy, then became a director in the Ministry of Revenue and served on the Grand Council staff.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶三年，典四川鄉試，督廣西學政，回京，仍直軍機。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiaqing he presided over the Sichuan provincial examination, supervised Guangxi education, returned to the capital, and still served on the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In 1798 he conducted the Sichuan provincial examinations, served as Guangxi education commissioner, and on returning to Beijing resumed Grand Council duty.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部郎中，調刑部，甚被眷遇。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Rites, moved to the Ministry of Justice, and was greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director in the Ministry of Rites, transferred to the Ministry of Justice, and enjoyed great imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 截取京察當外用，予升銜留任。

translations.literal: Selected in the capital evaluation for external appointment, he was granted elevated rank and retained in post.
translations.idiomatic: Marked for provincial appointment in the capital evaluation, he received an elevated rank and remained at his post.

sentences.zh: 十一年，詔嘉楷久直勤勉，以四五品京堂用。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year an edict praised Kai's long service and diligence and appointed him to fourth- or fifth-rank capital office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1806 an edict commended his long diligent service and appointed him to a fourth- or fifth-rank capital post.

sentences.zh: 歷太常寺少卿、光祿寺卿。

translations.literal: He served as Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 十二年，京師旱，疏請循漢書求雨閉陽縱陰之說，停止正陽門外石路工程，詔「修省在實政，無事傅會五行」，罷其奏。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the capital suffered drought; he memorialized requesting to follow the Han History's theory of seeking rain by closing yang and releasing yin, and stopping the stone road project outside Zhengyang Gate; an edict said "self-examination lies in real administration, there is no need to force-fit the Five Phases," and his memorial was rejected.
translations.idiomatic: In 1807, during a capital drought, he memorialized to follow Han-dynasty rain rituals and halt the stone road project outside Zhengyang Gate; the throne replied that reform lay in real governance, not forcing the Five Phases, and rejected his proposal.

sentences.zh: 迭命往河南、山西鞫獄，次第奏結，無枉縱。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly ordered to go to Henan and Shanxi to try cases, submitted conclusions in sequence, and neither wronged nor indulged.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly sent to try cases in Henan and Shanxi, he reported each conclusion in turn without injustice or leniency.

sentences.zh: 授河南布政使，十四年，護理巡撫，暫署河東河道總督。

translations.literal: He was appointed Henan Provincial Administration Commissioner; in the fourteenth year he acted as provincial governor and temporarily served as Hedong River Course Governor-General.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed Henan provincial administration commissioner, in 1809 he acted as governor and briefly as Hedong river course governor-general.

sentences.zh: 擢授廣西巡撫，尋調湖北。

translations.literal: He was promoted and appointed Guangxi Provincial Governor, and soon transferred to Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to governor of Guangxi, then transferred to Hubei.

sentences.zh: 十六年，疏言：「外洋鴉片煙入中國，奸商巧為夾帶。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he memorialized: "Foreign opium smoke enters China, and treacherous merchants skillfully smuggle it in concealment.
translations.idiomatic: In 1811 he memorialized: "Foreign opium enters China through merchants' smuggling.
