sentences.zh: 凡粵東西兩省匪類糾結，多由於此，以致盜風益熾。

translations.literal: All the bandit types of Guangdong's east and west two provinces who band together mostly arise from this, causing the wind of banditry to grow fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: Most banditry in eastern and western Guangdong stems from this trade, and robbery grows ever worse.

sentences.zh: 請飭閩、粵各關監督並近海督撫，嚴督關員盤檢，按律加等究辦。

translations.literal: He requested that supervisors of all Fujian and Guangdong customs and coastal provincial governors and governors strictly supervise customs officers in inspection, and investigate and punish according to law with increased severity.
translations.idiomatic: He asked Fujian and Guangdong customs supervisors and coastal governors to enforce rigorous inspections and punish violators to the full extent of the law.

sentences.zh: 內地貨賣一經發覺，窮究買自何人，來從何處，不得含糊搪塞，將失察偷漏監督委員及地方官一體參處，務使來踪盡絕，流弊自除，乃清理匪源之一端也。

translations.literal: Once inland sales were discovered, trace to whom purchased and whence it came, without vague evasion; impeach together supervisors, commissioners, and local officials who failed to detect smuggling and leakage, strive to cut off sources entirely so flowing abuses remove themselves—this is one means of clearing bandit sources.
translations.idiomatic: When inland sales were discovered, trace buyers and sources without evasion; impeach negligent supervisors and local officials; cut off supply entirely—that was one way to dry up banditry at its root.

sentences.zh: 」詔下沿海督撫認真察辦。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered coastal provincial governors and governors to investigate and handle earnestly.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict ordered coastal governors to enforce the policy rigorously.

sentences.zh: 授戶部侍郎，兼管錢法堂事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue and concurrently managed affairs of the Bureau of Monetary Standards.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice minister of revenue and concurrently directed the Bureau of Monetary Standards.

sentences.zh: 奏陳湖北地方事宜應酌劑者四端：請附近荊州糧米供支滿營兵食，餘俱改歸北漕；

translations.literal: He memorialized on four points in Hubei local affairs requiring deliberation: request grain from nearby Jingzhou to supply Manchu garrison soldiers' food, with the remainder all changed to northern grain transport;
translations.idiomatic: He proposed four reforms for Hubei: supply Manchu garrisons from nearby Jingzhou grain and route the rest to the northern tribute system;

sentences.zh: 沿江契買洲地，准其耕種納糧，無契者作為官地，召佃承種；

translations.literal: along the river contracted purchase of sandbar land, permit cultivation and tax payment; where there is no contract treat as government land and summon tenants to undertake planting;
translations.idiomatic: allow contracted sandbar land along the river to be farmed and taxed, and treat uncontracted land as government land leased to tenants;

sentences.zh: 新設提督，移駐襄陽府城；

translations.literal: the newly established provincial military commander should move his station to Xiangyang prefectural city;
translations.idiomatic: relocate the new provincial military commander to Xiangyang;

sentences.zh: 楚北均食淮鹽，襄陽、宜昌等府籌議減價。

translations.literal: northern Chu all consumes Huai salt; Xiangyang, Yichang, and other prefectures should deliberate reducing price.
translations.idiomatic: and study reducing Huai salt prices in Xiangyang, Yichang, and other northern Hubei prefectures.

sentences.zh: 下所司會議，惟沿江洲地一事照行，餘以窒礙置之。

translations.literal: It was referred to the responsible offices for deliberation; only the sandbar land along the river was implemented as proposed, the rest set aside as obstructed.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries deliberated; only the sandbar policy was adopted—the rest was set aside as impractical.

sentences.zh: 復出署河南巡撫。

translations.literal: He again went out to serve as acting Henan Provincial Governor.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as acting governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 匪徒王胯子句結南陽饑民滋事，成大獄。

translations.literal: Bandit Wang Kuazi colluded with Nanyang famine victims to make trouble, becoming a major case.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit Wang Kuazi incited Nanyang famine victims to riot, producing a major case.

sentences.zh: 楷至任，疏言：「前任巡撫恩長於南陽匪徒一案，前後具奏情節與原報不符，辦理過當。

translations.literal: When Kai took office he memorialized: "The former provincial governor En Chang in the Nanyang bandit case, in memorials before and after, presented circumstances not matching the original reports, and handled the matter excessively.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office, Qian memorialized that his predecessor En Chang had mishandled the Nanyang case—the facts in his reports did not match the original accounts and the punishments were excessive.

sentences.zh: 府、州、縣等緝犯並未廢弛，平日聲名尚好，現擬絞監候之二十餘犯，明年秋審，均應情實，不敢知而不言。

translations.literal: Prefectural, departmental, and county officials in pursuing criminals had not been lax; their reputations on ordinary days were still good; the more than twenty offenders now proposed for strangulation with delayed execution, at next year's autumn review, should all be actual cases—I dare not know and not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials had not neglected pursuit of criminals and had good reputations; the more than twenty men now awaiting execution after autumn review were all guilty in fact—I could not remain silent.

sentences.zh: 」詔以「句決與否，臨時自有權衡，非臣下所可豫定。

translations.literal: " An edict stated: "Whether to execute immediately or not, at the moment there is one's own weighing—this is not what subordinates may predetermine.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne replied: "Whether to execute is decided at the moment by imperial discretion—not something a subject may prejudge.

sentences.zh: 地方官咎有應得，豈能開復？

translations.literal: Local officials' blame is deserved—how can they be restored?
translations.idiomatic: Local officials deserve blame—how can they be rehabilitated?

sentences.zh: 」斥楷敷陳未當，近於喜事。

translations.literal: " Kai was rebuked for presenting matters improperly, approaching meddling in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " Qian was rebuked for improper presentation and meddling.

sentences.zh: 調補工部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to fill the post of Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 尋授安徽巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Anhui Provincial Governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed governor of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 以歙縣監生張良璧採生斃命，命楷親訊，讞擬未依凌遲律，失於輕比，部議降一級調用，改降二級留任。

translations.literal: Because She County student Zhang Liangbi caused death while gathering medicinal materials, Kai was ordered to try the case in person; the proposed verdict did not follow the lingering-death statute and erred in light comparison; the ministry deliberated demotion one rank and transfer, changed to demotion two ranks retained in post.
translations.idiomatic: When She County student Zhang Liangbi caused a death while gathering herbs, Qian was ordered to try the case; his verdict failed to apply the lingering-death statute and was deemed too lenient—the ministry demoted him two ranks but kept him in office.

sentences.zh: 十七年，卒。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1812.

sentences.zh: 詔以「楷直樞曹久，有勞，自簡封圻，治理安靜。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "Kai long served directly in the secretariat with merit; from selection to frontier posts, his governance was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Qian served long and diligently on the Grand Council; in provincial office his governance was tranquil.

sentences.zh: 母程年逾七旬，嗣子尚幼，深憫之，特賜卹。

translations.literal: His mother Cheng was over seventy, his heir son still young—the court deeply pitied this and specially granted condolence payments.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Cheng was over seventy and his heir still a child; the court pitied them and granted special funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 和舜武，伊拉里氏，滿洲鑲藍旗人。

translations.literal: He Shunwu, of the Ilari clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He Shunwu, of the Ilari clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 官學生，考授太常寺筆帖式。

translations.literal: A government school student, through examination he was appointed a clerk in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: A government school graduate, he passed examination and was appointed a clerical secretary in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 累遷步軍統領衙門員外郎。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Vice Commissioner in the Metropolitan Infantry Commandant's Yamen.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice commissioner in the Metropolitan Infantry Command.

sentences.zh: 以治獄明獲議敘，遷兵部郎中，兼公中佐領。

translations.literal: Because he handled cases clearly he received deliberation for commendation, was transferred to Director in the Ministry of War, and concurrently served as garrison assistant commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Recognized for clear handling of cases, he became director in the Ministry of War and assistant commandant of a garrison company.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十五年，出為江蘇鹽法道。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Jiaqing he went out as Jiangsu Salt Administration Circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In 1810 he was posted as Jiangsu salt administration intendant.

sentences.zh: 累遷山東布政使，整飭吏治，輿論歸之。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Shandong Provincial Administration Commissioner, rectified official administration, and public opinion rallied to him.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Shandong provincial administration commissioner, rectified official conduct, and won public acclaim.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，擢山西巡撫，調河南。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was promoted to Shanxi Provincial Governor and transferred to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1817 he was promoted to governor of Shanxi, then transferred to Henan.

sentences.zh: 會布政使吳邦慶疏請於漳、衛合流之處建閘壩，和舜武謂：「漳河盛漲湍悍，非一閘所能禦，越閘旁趨，且停蓄泥沙，塞衛水宣洩之路。

translations.literal: When Provincial Administration Commissioner Wu Bangqing memorialized requesting construction of a sluice dam where the Zhang and Wei rivers join, He Shunwu said: "When the Zhang River swells its current is fierce and violent; one sluice cannot withstand it; it would bypass the sluice and rush aside, and moreover detain silt and mud, blocking the Wei River's path of discharge.
translations.idiomatic: When Administration Commissioner Wu Bangqing proposed a sluice where the Zhang and Wei rivers meet, He argued: "The Zhang in flood is too fierce for a single sluice; water would bypass it, deposit silt, and block the Wei's drainage.

sentences.zh: 」疏請罷之，仍舊章每年挑濬竇公河以資鹽運，如所議行。

translations.literal: " He memorialized requesting abolition of it, and following old regulations annually dredging Dougong River to support salt transport, as he proposed and was implemented.
translations.idiomatic: " He memorialized to abandon the project and continue annual dredging of the Dougong River for salt transport, as adopted.

sentences.zh: 逾年，調山東。

translations.literal: After a year he was transferred to Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was transferred to Shandong.

sentences.zh: 仁宗聞其前為布政使有聲，故有此授。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong heard that he had earlier as provincial administration commissioner had a reputation, and therefore made this appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong appointed him because of his reputation as Shandong administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 山東民俗好訟，又近畿，輒走訴京師。

translations.literal: Shandong local custom favored litigation, and being near the metropolitan periphery, people often ran to sue in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong was litigious and, being near the capital, people often took cases to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 和舜武再蒞，訟頓減，特詔褒勉。

translations.literal: When He Shunwu came again, lawsuits suddenly decreased, and a special edict praised and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: On his return lawsuits dropped sharply, and the emperor issued special commendation.

sentences.zh: 疏請清理京控積案，責巡撫、籓、臬分提鞫訊，月定課程，各自陳奏；

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting clearing accumulated capital-appeal cases, charging provincial governors, treasuries, and surveillance commissioners to take turns interrogating, setting monthly schedules, each reporting separately;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to clear the backlog of capital appeals, assigning governors, treasurers, and surveillance commissioners monthly quotas for investigation and reporting;

sentences.zh: 又請酌​​改竊盜窩匪條例，加重定擬，俟盜風稍戢，復舊：並從之。

translations.literal: he also requested deliberating alteration of statutes on theft, bandit dens, and nests, with heavier sentencing, to restore the old when the wind of banditry slightly subsided: all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: and asked to stiffen penalties for theft and bandit dens until crime subsided, then restore former statutes—all approved.

sentences.zh: 至年終，審結積案千餘起，予優敘。

translations.literal: By year's end more than a thousand accumulated cases were tried and concluded, and he was granted superior commendation.
translations.idiomatic: By year's end he had cleared more than a thousand backlog cases and received superior commendation.

sentences.zh: 京察复予議敘。

translations.literal: At the capital evaluation he again received deliberation for commendation.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital personnel review he again received commendation.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，卒，上甚惜之，優詔賜卹，贈總督銜，諡恭慎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he died; the emperor deeply regretted it, granted superior edict condolence payments, posthumously granted governor-general rank, and gave the posthumous title Gongjin.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1819; the emperor mourned him deeply, granted superior funeral honors, posthumously made him governor-general, and titled him Gongjin.

sentences.zh: 論曰：仁宗初政，特重廉吏。

translations.literal: The commentary says: At the beginning of Renzong's administration, incorrupt officials were especially valued.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: At the start of Emperor Renzong's reign, honest officials were especially prized.

sentences.zh: 岳起、荊道乾清操實政為之冠；

translations.literal: Yue Qi and Jing Daoqian, with pure conduct and real administration, were the foremost;
translations.idiomatic: Yue Qi and Jing Daoqian led them all in integrity and effective government;

sentences.zh: 謝啟昆、張師誠才猷建樹，卓越一時：並專圻碩望矣。

translations.literal: Xie Qikun and Zhang Shicheng, with talent and strategy and established achievements, were outstanding for a time: all were great hopes of their frontier posts.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Qikun and Zhang Shicheng were men of outstanding talent and achievement in their day—great provincial hopes every one.

sentences.zh: 李殿圖、李奕疇、錢楷亦各以明慎慈惠見稱，和舜武課最簿書，遂邀易名曠典；

translations.literal: Li Diantu, Li Yichou, and Qian Kai were also each praised for clarity, caution, and kindness; He Shunwu excelled in evaluating records and documents, and thereby received the rare honor of a posthumous title;
translations.idiomatic: Li Diantu, Li Yichou, and Qian Kai were praised for judicial clarity and kindness; He Shunwu excelled in administrative metrics and won the rare honor of a posthumous title;

sentences.zh: 王紹蘭一眚坐廢，晚成經學：殆有幸有不幸哉？

translations.literal: Wang Shaolan, through one fault, was dismissed and in later years completed classical learning: perhaps there is fortune within misfortune?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shaolan was ruined by a single fault yet became a classical scholar in retirement—is that fortune within misfortune?
